name: Tammy Baldwin
subject: This is why I got into public service
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TAMMY BALDWIN FOR SENATE
body:
| I’ve fought against Republicans’ efforts to repeal the ACA before, and I won’t back down now.
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/67?t=1&akid=2812%2E35263%2EABKXah)
Peter — Growing up, I was diagnosed with a serious illness and spent three months in the hospital. [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2155?c0=tbe-em-jun24.Hijekx&refcode=AU_STB_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20240613_AM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=2812%2E35263%2EABKXah) When I recovered, my grandparents, who raised me, searched for an insurance policy that would cover me in the future. They wanted to make sure I was protected in case I got sick again, but they couldn’t find any policies. Not from any insurer. Not at any price. All because I had been labeled as a child with a _"pre-existing condition."_ That meant my grandparents had to pay for my health care out of pocket — and they had to make significant sacrifices to do so. **That’s why I got into public service.** My story isn’t a unique one. I’m one of 133 million Americans who have the "pre-existing condition" label attached to our care — and before the _Affordable Care Act_ was passed, many of us could be denied coverage. Now, insurance companies can no longer discriminate against someone based on their pre-existing condition. I championed health reform and wrote the amendment to allow young people to stay on their parent’s insurance plan up to age 26. These policy changes have led to millions more Americans getting the health insurance they need. So you can imagine my frustration when Republicans like my opponent threaten to repeal the ACA, which would strip away coverage from millions of Americans. If Republicans flip this seat and take back the Senate, the ACA will be on the chopping block and countless Americans could find themselves in a place where insurance companies, once again, write all the rules. I’ve fought against Republicans’ efforts to repeal the ACA before, and I won’t back down now. **But I can't do it alone, Peter. I need your help to keep up this fight in the U.S. Senate.** **[Will you make a donation to my reelection campaign and help defend our Democratic Senate majority? It’s the only way we’ll prevent Republicans from rolling back our progress and advancing their far-right agenda.](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2155?c0=tbe-em-jun24.Hijekx&refcode=AU_STB_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20240613_AM1_V1_S1&t=5&akid=2812%2E35263%2EABKXah)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | [CHIP IN $5 NOW](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3663?c0=tbe-em-jun24.xQpXoA&refcode=AU_STB_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20240613_AM1_V1_S1&t=6&akid=2812%2E35263%2EABKXah)

Supreme Court Backs Full Access to Widely Used Abortion Pill**

Peter, this is great news for a lot of reasons...**but let's be clear:** This decision should have NEVER been up for debate in the first place.

[**Rush a donation if you agree: We need to codify our reproductive rights in Congress this fall by kicking extremists out and replacing them with real representation in Washington (and beyond).**](https://an.collectivepac.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvJB22Yj9KNp6Q7r_1N-iSE7OCFp1R-1l_ZYqJIkjojO0WgZ-71YF_sQWbt8Z5psdQkphrs9b0P3ZKEb84UjFglv2D1BdyNRsV7tEM8SjePI_xGeyRjvq-d7zmiKBk3V8B5LNej0LbazxIRvNoOvLfsNkDS4EuoYF2uLbT1COgqbGkspbEHWN8Fizd1IJ5sqkUEhl9H5D84EL3KXvnYhS7PkOrWKWFlstvIlHXWrg4Z8Fp5ot_PjK6xGioNXK5jJs9mX7nqjP2kGsgQT2yaOQd-E87nG9b7CwBxZghBB1nAd2o6ZNVFYpZweJ24HqvzRlmQGpV0lSyccQTjzV1QKCVvgxvrEIFpW29BlBhdCUbGdeBCt1K9R9-aD2rm7c9AxziBu6CTVkQG8WFJjKv-RifRMBUYOfg1u73XIVUBzjzp6A/476/ZzOVQWTMTqKdK-Ze6eiC-A/h1/h001.TFFbFBuk4AsVeK7MeeLvdO_XTxlGbebBgORtd3AMow4)

Today is one more example of why politicians need to stay out of decisions about abortion, and why we need to guarantee abortion access nationally. But the only way that happens is if we elect politicians who care about our bodily autonomy.

body:
Everything they've told us is a lie

|
---
Hunter Biden has just been found guilty on federal weapons charges.

Remember his laptop?

They told us it was fake. They even suppressed the story to swing the election to Joe. Turns out It was real.

Then they told us the transcripts showing that Joe Biden was in on his son's corruption were nothing to worry about. They were.

They even told us the "art deals" to Biden's mega donors were totally normal. They aren't.

[**Everything the establishment has told us about the Biden family's corruption has been a lie. Now that Hunter has been found guilty on federal weapons charges, we're one step closer to getting justice. But we can't stop now. Joe and Hunter MUST be held accountable for selling out our country to the highest bidder. Peter,

The U.S. Supreme Court did the right thing today and denied standing to a group of anti-choice extremists who challenged the FDA's approval of mifepristone, an important part of the medication abortion protocol that has been safely used by millions of people for decades.

**But here's the thing: This attack on our rights should never have gotten this far, and millions of Americans still live in states with total abortion bans.**

**We know** Republicans will try anything to restrict our reproductive freedom, and this ruling won't stop them on their mission.

**We know** the majority of Americans are pro-choice.

https://karenforvirginia.com/ [https://karenforvirginia.com/] Karen Jenkins for HB-89

name: Josh Stein (personal)
subject: Let me introduce myself, folks.
body:
Friend,

I’m writing today with updates from the campaign trail, and important news coming out of North Carolina (like how I’m officially the Democratic nominee for Governor and recent polling shows our campaign in a statistical TIE with my far-right opponent!). And yes, this email will ask you to donate at the end. If you already know how important it is to hit our fundraising goals, you can click here to make a split contribution to my campaign and Wes Moore now.

[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1]

Today, I wanted to let you know who I am and why I am in this tough race in the first place.

My name is Josh Stein. I am a father, a husband, a proud North Carolinian, and the current Attorney General of our state. And I am running for Governor of North Carolina.

For the past seven years as your Attorney General, I’ve taken on big fights for the people of North Carolina and won. I’ve worked hard to keep families safe, hold corporate wrongdoers accountable for the damage they’ve done to our people, make polluters pay to clean up the messes they make, and defend your reproductive and voting rights.

I’ve stood up to the radical right who are trying to take away our freedoms. Because the bottom line is this: North Carolina is a great place to live – and we must do everything we can to protect the state we love and the people who live here.

Now, I am running for Governor of North Carolina because we’re facing a real threat. My opponent Mark Robinson is a far-right extremist who wants to tell you who you can love ... and who you should hate.

Despite how wrong Robinson is for our state, we’re in a statistical dead heat in the polls.

We always knew this race would be a close one — statewide races in North Carolina always are. Hitting our goals is crucial to our efforts to fight back against extremism in our state and win this election.

Today, I am asking for your help to keep our campaign on track. Please, click here or on a button below to donate to my campaign and Wes Moore. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1]

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation will go through immediately:
Donate $10 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1-el&express_lane=true&amount=10]
Donate $25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1-el&express_lane=true&amount=25]
Donate $50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1-el&express_lane=true&amount=50]
Donate $75 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1-el&express_lane=true&amount=75]
Donate $100 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1-el&express_lane=true&amount=100]
Other Amount [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1-el-other]

The future of our state is on the line, but with your help, we can continue to make progress for North Carolina and defeat extremism.

Thank you,

Josh Stein

And while my campaign is over, my mission to protect our democracy from the most extreme threats is not. My top priority this election begins at the top of our ballots: re-electing President Biden. We either re-elect a Democrat with a record of fighting for voting rights, Social Security, healthcare and more. Or we re-elect a 34-time convicted felon who incited a deadly insurrection on the Capitol. [I chose option A. But Donald Trump hauled in over $141 MILLION after his conviction, so we have to fight back. Grassroots donors chipping in $10 or $20 at a time to help our #1 Democracy Defender, President Biden, will make a huge difference. Can you rush a donation now?](https://default.salsalabs.org/T69d5f68c-4d50-45d5-a549-e73fc28f18c1/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

Early voting continues today! **[If you haven’t voted yet, find your polling location here, make a plan, and VOTE!](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/8c30722d3644710666a6b3c4b83ff292/45443/4e86f9e0ab9e35a53947229f28c3afba/cfcdc5ce78d978cfc3d6b838967d376c/45443)** When I’m on the campaign trail, a lot of folks ask what the differences are between Brian Jack and me. Truth is, we’re both conservatives who support President Trump. **But when it comes to experience, it’s a different story. ** **Here’s what I mean.**
---
---
**When it comes to who knows this district,** we lived and worked here, raised our family here, went to school here, and go to church here. Brian Jack has spent his career in DC and has never paid property taxes in Georgia. **When it comes to where our support is coming from,** the huge majority of our donations are from right here in the 3rd District. 97.4% of Brian Jack’s are not. **When it comes to experience getting things done,** I’ve served as an Army Ranger, created economic growth as a businessman, and written conservative policies that became law as a Georgia Senator. **Brian Jack sat in the room while decisions were made. I’ve been the one in the room making the decisions.** In times of crisis, we need proven resilience. That’s the contrast in this race. And I’d be honored to earn your vote, and to serve you, in Congress. **[If you want to volunteer in the campaign’s final days, click here to email Ben Jarrard, my campaign manager.](mailto:ben@votemikedugan.com "ben@votemikedugan.com")** Let’s go!

Peter,

We have incredible news.

The Supreme Court just announced its decision to reject a Texas law that would have taken mifepristone, an FDA-approved medication, off the market. This means women will still have access to this safe, viable medication for abortion care.

This decision by SCOTUS couldn't come at a more important time. Extreme Republicans in states across the country have doubled down on their efforts to restrict women's rights and reproductive freedoms.

Twenty-seven states now have a limit on abortion starting as early as six weeks, while fourteen states have near-complete abortion bans with few exceptions. If mifepristone was removed from the market, it would have had devastating consequences for women who just want access to the care they need.

As the first woman doctor in Congress, Kim will always fight for access to reproductive healthcare because she knows politics has no place in the examination room. Yet if Republicans had their way, millions of women would be deprived of the ability to make the most important decisions of their lives on their own. That's why Kim keeps fighting for abortion rights to this very day.

Peter: this may be a win for women’s healthcare, but anti-abortion activists will use their fury from this ruling to reignite their efforts for a full abortion ban. That's why we have to take back the majority to codify abortion rights once and for all.

My #transparencyproject journey started on February 17, 2022, which was the day of my 52nd birthday. More significant for this story, this also happened to be the day that we lost a great American Patriot, [Congressman Jim Hagedorn](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c8da68f5-1663-415b-9ccb-35658420514e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). For three short months following the untimely death of the Congressman, I made the decision to run to replace him in Congress, set up a first-rate campaign team, raised significant money, participated in a nominating convention, and ran in a primary election that covered 21 counties in Southern Minnesota. We all know that this effort did not end with me representing the great folks here in Washington, D.C. Despite this outcome, I was thrilled to have had the experience of "being in the arena" meeting fantastic people and holding the banner high advocating for a better community.
I did not expect that a series of requests for public data sent during the whirlwind of my campaign would propel me on a trajectory through the maze of bureaucracy, searching for transparency surrounding the task of counting votes in our elections. I have been documenting this effort through a series of writings I have labelled the "transparencyproject". A full compilation of these [updates](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2e28b4dd-f8e7-4546-82ae-c0f1b650376c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) can be found on my profile page at my law office. Starting in October, 2023 I also found my way to the Substack platform [(@bendasense](https://substack.com/@bendasense?utm_source=profile-page)) which provides a wonderful outlet to create and distribute substantive content greater that 170 characters. My non-profit "Benda for Congress" has now evolved into "Benda for Commonsense" which I describe as, "my outlet to tilt against group think, with the goal of bringing some small-town common-sense to the world!!
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/343e8bb6-2d97-4aba-907b-540bab7a834c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I am currently following the bread-crumbs that slip out from behind the curtain of secrecy in our election process. I recently realized that I am effectively performing "investigative lawyering", like "investigative journalism." I described the heightened need for this scrutiny in one of my previous posts:
> Election officials hold election data in trust on behalf of the public, not to the exclusion of the public. Transparency from, and accountability of our election officials should be embedded into the system. The rapid evolution of technology in the election process quickens the need to normalize public transparency.
My current legal journey started in August 2022 in Rice County District Court and is now [up for review](https://open.substack.com/pub/bendasense/p/we-are-going-to-the-minnesota-supreme?r=1rusnm&utm_campaign=post&utm_medium=web) by the Minnesota Supreme Court. This experience has provided clarity to me that we must insist on an atmosphere of transparency and accountability regarding all public institutions.
This legal action focuses on what I consider the illegal use of modems to transmit early election results to the Secretary of State's Office. Counties are authorized to transmit early election results from precincts to the County Office. That, however, is the end of the line for the transmission of these results. In what I advocate is a clear violation of the [law](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e4e8c2d2-3138-46ba-b7db-9e6b5eebce6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Hennepin, Anoka, Washington, Rice, Cass, Stearns, and Carver Counties all take the additional step of transmitting these early results to the Secretary of State. I started questioning this process over two years ago - why is everything so secretive? When are these early results transmitted to the Secretary and who has access to view them? Sunshine is clearly needed! I will be asking the Minnesota Supreme Court to allow this scrutiny to continue.
I hope to inspire others to also become engaged, to ask questions, and not simply accept the bureaucratic status quo. The #transparencyproject is a public hashtag that symbolizes my journey. Please feel free to use it for your own journey. For me, the quest for transparency and accountability will continue...
Matt Benda
Albert Lea Attorney and Community Advocate

Hi Peter,

We want to draw your attention to Nebraska – where, last year, a legislature made up of 71% men passed an abortion ban.

[**We don’t believe men should be the ones making laws about women’s bodies – that’s why we are proud to announce our endorsements of pro-choice women who need our help as they run for winnable seats in Nebraska. Will you help us fight for abortion protections in Nebraska by chipping in $20.24 or more today?**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/86827189/479149353/-1569524446?refcode=EM_F_240613NE_N_CD_90DO_10_NG_TestB_L1&amount=20.24&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYyMDE4ZjY1LWE2MjktZWYxMS04NmQyLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=eiLJsO5Iv271BSfVgtrzWqUD61IqYr7ovtPrBcv6BrI=)

✅ **Carol Blood is running for Congressional District 1 in Nebraska.** Carol has served as an elected official over the last 16 years on both the City Council and the Nebraska Legislature. She has been an active volunteer and advocate for women since 1992.

Carol’s opponent deeply **supports a complete and total ban on abortion.** In fact, during his first term in the Nebraska Legislature, he introduced and successfully passed the Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act, **the _nation's first_ abortion ban, _nearly a decade ago._** Meanwhile, Carol believes that safe and accessible reproductive healthcare is a basic right that is supported by science, medicine, and respect for human dignity.

✅ **Maggie Douglas is running for election to the Nebraska State Board of Education.** Maggie is committed to ensuring education is equitable and accessible for all students, promoting policies that boost teacher retention, encouraging parent engagement, and keeping schools safe. She firmly believes that every student should have the resources they need to learn and succeed, no matter where they come from or their life situation. As an educator, Maggie’s experience will guide her in making the best decisions for her constituents and the students of Nebraska.

Book bans and transhuman rights are currently the top issues in this district. Maggie is against book bans and has been vocal about keeping book decisions at the local level. Her opponent has ties to Moms for Liberty and the backing of their state's Republican party.

[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/86827192/479149359/-1569524446?refcode=EM_F_240613NE_N_CD_90DO_10_NG_TestB_P2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYyMDE4ZjY1LWE2MjktZWYxMS04NmQyLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=eiLJsO5Iv271BSfVgtrzWqUD61IqYr7ovtPrBcv6BrI=)
---
✅ **Mary Ann Folchert is running for Nebraska State Legislature, District 31.** Mary Ann believes that every woman deserves access to comprehensive reproductive healthcare, including abortion. As she stated in our endorsement interview, _“Healthcare decisions should be patient-centered and based on scientific and medical understanding, not the religious or moral preferences of lawmakers.”_

Meanwhile, she is challenging the current Senator, Kathleen Kauth, a partisan Republican politician who helped craft a bill that restricted access to abortion after 9 weeks as well as access to gender-affirming care for minors.

Hello, in just a minute I’ll ask you to split a contribution between my campaign and Debbie Mucarsel-Powell's ahead of our critical mid-month deadline, but first I hope you’ll give me a moment to explain why it’s so important to give — especially today.
I grew up on my family’s farm, and Sharla and I still work that land today. In my opinion, being a farmer makes me a better senator. My background is a big part of the reason I remain grounded and focused on defending our Montana way of life. Because with all the chaos in Washington (especially now), you need somebody who will roll up their sleeves and get to work.
Last time I ran, nearly $70 million was spent on the Montana Senate race. This time around, we’ve already passed that number: **A****n eye-popping $120 million has been spent or reserved in advertising alone.** It’ll take a lot of support from this team to raise what we’ll need to protect this seat.
And if you know me, I’m not the kind of person who likes to ask for money. But I bet Mitch McConnell would be _furious_ if we showed him that a whole lot of grassroots power is stronger than his wealthy donors and super PACs will ever be.
Let’s be clear: **This election isn’t a sure thing.** Experts say this race is a toss-up and rank Montana as one of the seats most likely to flip. That’s why it’s SO important you make a contribution today — everything is on the line.
Everyone — including Mitch McConnell — is watching what we raise to judge the strength of this team. **I don’t expect you to chip in every time I ask, but I need you on my side now more than ever to show our opponents we’re ready to fight back and win.**

BREAKING: Supreme Court rejects challenge to abortion pill mifepristone, allowing drug to stay on the market **BREAKING:** Supreme Court rejects challenge to abortion pill mifepristone, allowing drug to stay on the market
_“The ruling is a significant setback for the anti-abortion movement in what was the first major Supreme Court case on reproductive rights since the court’s conservative majority overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022.”_ Peter,

In a unanimous 9-0 decision, the Supreme Court ruled to uphold access to mifepristone, the medication commonly used in medication abortions.

Today’s ruling is a crucial win for the majority of Americans who believe in the right to choose and the necessity of safe and legal abortion care. It is a testament to our ongoing fight for reproductive justice, and the tireless work of advocates across the country.

But Peter, while we celebrate this victory, we can’t forget that this is the same Supreme Court that overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , striking down decades of settled law that protected a woman's right to choose. **The fight for reproductive rights is far from over. We can expect the challenges to women’s autonomy over their bodies from extremist, anti-choice justices and politicians to continue.**

In Congress, I will ALWAYS stand with the pro-choice majority of Americans – and St. Louisans – who believe that healthcare decisions should be left between a person and their doctor, including the right to have an abortion. **I am committed to defending and expanding reproductive freedom,** and will fight against any attempts to roll back our rights in the House.

Thank you for your ongoing support.

In solidarity,

Dear Peter,

We thought you may be interested to receive this CONSERVATIVE NEWS ALERT from Illinois Review (https://www.illinoisreview.com/?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d0b6a06e79-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) .

DEFLECTING DON: IL GOP Chair Fails Leadership Test, Conveniently Hides Behind Party Rules as Calls Grow for Mark Shaw's Resignation (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/06/deflecting-don-il-gop-chair-fails-leadership-test-conveniently-hides-behind-party-rules-as-calls-grow-for-mark-shaws-resignation.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d0b6a06e79-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/06/deflecting-don-il-gop-chair-fails-leadership-test-conveniently-hides-behind-party-rules-as-calls-grow-for-mark-shaws-resignation.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d0b6a06e79-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D

By Illinois Review
Like a scene out of the movie The Skulls, where Senator Ames Levritt tells a group of young men, “Our rules supersede those of the outside world” – embattled Illinois Republican Party Chairman Don Tracy, in a letter to Lake County GOP Central Committee Chairman Keith Brin on Wednesday, conveniently hid behind party rules stating that he did not have the authority to remove Mark Shaw as vice chairman despite the party changing its rules during the state convention last month to allow Tracy’s close friend and ally Vince Kolber (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/06/breaking-vince-kolber-who-votes-in-il-wi-resigns-as-il-gop-finance-chairman-blames-grassroots-for-his-downfall.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d0b6a06e79-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) , who votes in both Illinois and Wisconsin, to remain on the ballot for national committeeman despite failing to meet the candidacy requirements as outlined by the IL GOP’s own bylaws.

On Monday,
Brin (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/06/calls-mount-for-ilgop-shake-up-amid-mark-shaw-fake-delegate-scandal.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d0b6a06e79-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) – who replaced Shaw as chairman, wrote a letter calling on all 102 county GOP leaders to demand Shaw’s resignation or removal, writing, “We have crossed a rubicon.” On Wednesday, Tracy responded to Brin’s letter, writing, “I have done my best to remain neutral in this process because, based on the bylaws of the Illinois Republican Party, it is the sole purview of the seventeen (17) individual members of the State Central Committee to elect and remove a Vice-Chair.”

Tracy and many state party leaders have always placed an emphasis on money over people – and as a result, the Illinois Republican Party – and under Tracy’s leadership, has slipped further into irrelevance as the Democrats continue to expand their super majority control in both the Illinois House and Senate – and control every statewide office – leaving Republicans voiceless on local and state matters. And for major donors like Vince Kolber and Mark Shaw – rules and party bylaws can be broken – because, as Tracy has proven, “our rules supersede those of the outside world.”

Immediately after Tracy’s letter went public, Brin – in an exclusive statement and shared with this publication, said, “I read the chairman’s letter and I agree that we need Party unity. However, I think the only way to achieve Party unity is for the state central committee to remove Mark Shaw.”

State Rep. Jed Davis (Dist. 75) and the chair of the Kendall County Republican Party, posted, “I stand with Keith Brin. Mark Shaw should resign from his position in party leadership. There’s no excuse for casting illegal votes during our state convention.”

Much is made of America's primary system being broken, and that conventional view is correct: primaries are [low-turnout elections](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f7ecabe6-b0c3-40fd-9a75-99c303520433?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that basically give the most partisan voters an extra vote. Primaries tend to select candidates who [are more extreme than and less representative of the electorate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/053efd40-5325-4ba3-ad31-02f2a0f69574?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Based on [ratings from Cook Political Report](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/69e63b2a-b677-4ec3-9f3f-efa012d899fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), there are 69 competitive1 House seats at the moment, which means that 84% of House seats are functionally decided in the primary. If you remove the Likely Democrat and Likely Republican seats, that number pops to 90%.2
Subscribe to receive new posts about politics--and where conventional wisdom is wrong.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTQ1Mjk4MzA5LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzE4MzAwODM5LCJleHAiOjE3MjA4OTI4MzksImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.0-FvUp8WKA5U8_2x8q3EA2HBY9UEfdel5o4zNyaamSU?)
There are a lot of reasons why so few seats are competitive, stemming largely from [the way that states draw their Congressional maps](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/548db37b-4ea8-4c13-8af2-e9b3428f44d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--something [I am way more familiar with than most](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5ca00a00-a59a-4d8c-845d-d1a5cfbb142d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
But here is what's **Not Quite Right ...** Most Americans can vote in the primaries of their choosing. If you're a Democrat, there's no shame in crossing over and grabbing a Republican ticket. In many cases, it's strategic.
### Get out and vote (where it matters)
According to my back-of-the-envelope math,3 at least two-thirds of Americans aren't restricted when deciding which party's primary to vote in. In most states, that means you can request either a Republican or a Democratic ticket,4 regardless of who you've voted for in the past or any party affiliation you have.5
Let's say that you live in a state like Hawaii, which has open primaries. Hawaii is, almost uniformly these days, a Democratic state.6 And yet [some 75,000+ people chose to vote in a Republican primary](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a6c2fcf1-9084-4483-a1f6-c36ccd4ddd47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that was entirely meaningless.
I am sure that most of those people were committed Republicans who find Democrats thoroughly objectionable. But they could've voted in the Democratic primary and had a say in picking a candidate _more_ palatable to them, even if they don't actually like them.
Instead, they took time off work, went to their polling place, and in almost every election, got to choose who had the honor of finishing a distant second to the inevitable Democratic winner.7
### Missourians (and others), pick a winner!
Like most of the people on this list, I live and vote in Missouri. And in Missouri, as much as I wish it weren't the case, there aren't a lot of races lately where voting on the Democratic side makes much of a difference.8
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/44dc8fcf-7329-47f2-a813-2c1471176a69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Missouri, despite [repeated efforts to close its primaries](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/64d16074-698d-4371-bf57-721b5e5e1bc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), allows voters to pick any primary ballot they want when they go to vote. **So: while I am not a Republican, I will be grabbing a Republican ballot come[August 6](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/66b7f254-84e7-467b-8fdc-4a5b39a05a5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
Unless you live in Missouri's 1st Congressional District and have the opportunity to vote for [Wesley Bell](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/83005984-58ce-405d-80a3-ad5ae2d3461c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),9 **I would encourage you to grab the Republican ballot too.** Whoever wins the Republican primary will almost certainly be the winner come November; this way, you can at least vote for people who are the least crazy, the least anti-democracy, and the most pragmatic in their approach to politics.10
To vote in the Democratic primary is something like voting in Hawaii's Republican primary: you're offering input on who gets to finish in a robust second place.
You still won't like a lot of what they do. But at least you'll have had _some_ input. Though it doesn't always feel like it, **not all Republicans are created equal.** 11
### Some final thoughts
* If you live in one of these states, with open or semi-open primaries, always grab the primary ballot of the party whose candidates win elections: Alabama, Arkansas, Hawaii, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maine, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, North Dakota, Ohio, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Texas, and Vermont.12
* This doesn't betray your values as a Democrat, and this doesn't preclude you from voting for Democrats in November, like I will. But it gives you a say in deciding who your all-but-certain representatives will be.
* In the next edition of Not Quite Right... I will talk about what's going on with younger voters, and how all over the world, [young men and young women are all of a sudden voting in drastically different ways](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/900bd6c2-4cb8-4cca-a95d-565f1192374d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Finally, please take a moment to fill out this survey. I'd love your thoughts and ideas.
[Start Survey](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6112c32f-798e-4b6f-bf59-6167c0dc02ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
1
Meaning, simply, that both a Democrat and a Republican have a realistic shot of winning.
2
There are groups like the [Welcome PAC](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6d4e5c87-c724-4925-824c-adc59bb2cf3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who I work with, that try to find competitive races which, despite conventional wisdom, Democrats can win with the right candidates. That's a critical part of winning back a U.S. House majority. But it doesn't change the fact that primaries almost always decide elections.
3
Taking the info from the [two](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/96d63cc9-556a-47c1-ba1d-b824f1132627?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [different](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8f403866-916b-4dbf-948e-1a3b3ffaa406?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wikipedia pages, and then hoping I did my Excel math right.
4
Or Libertarian, Green, Constitution, etc.
5
A few states--Alaska, California, Louisiana, and Washington state, I believe--have candidates from all parties on the same primary ballot, which makes things easier.
6
Every statewide elected official is a Democrat. Hawaii has [76 state legislators](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7fde1878-60a7-4a6e-ac57-50d852966e58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): 68 Democrats and eight Republicans. You get the idea.
7
For what it's worth, about 75% of votes cast in Hawaii's primary were in the Democratic primary even though the Governor ultimately won only ("only") [63% of the vote](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/54acf8ba-39cf-46db-ad72-4337a4621e8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), suggesting that some Republicans were strategic with their primary votes.
8
Nicole Galloway is the one Democratic exception. She had the fortune of running against a [flawed Republican in 2018](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d722defa-2918-4b6d-8eb9-9100a49eb7d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and then she [lost in her bid for Governor in 2020](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e0b78217-95a4-412b-923b-528186c53e46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
9
If you _do_ live in the 1st Congressional District, you'll have the ability to vote in the primary between [Wesley Bell](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/64082f8c-d806-45c7-889d-3e55518bd029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and Rep. Cori Bush. I may write more on this later, but I'm full-throated in my endorsement of Wesley Bell and would encourage all of you reading this who live in the 1st Congressional District to pick up a Democratic ballot and vote for him. Beyond [Wesley's impressive bona fides](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b30b1ec0-3003-4216-aff8-b9de4f66ba0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Cori Bush is bad for the district: she's voted against [infrastructure investment](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/568f846f-48e4-40b0-97b4-9132fefcfe21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [public safety](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/56649929-7f26-4696-96be-f399874359e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [jobs](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e71f2739-5882-4b76-990c-a4837801c92c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). She's [under investigation for misusing taxpayer money](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d972bc67-ac2f-4115-b2a8-47f048f45f96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to line her own pockets. She's shown no interest in legislating. If she isn't outright lying about what she's done for the district, [at the very least she's grossly exaggerating](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/00c46292-e202-486a-9c02-e8dc90af3ebc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Polls [have her down significantly](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/87f118b7-722e-4021-8919-ba308d28a470?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and Wesley Bell will make a very good and very effective representative for St. Louis in Congress. Here's a link to donate to Wesley Bell, if you can't vote for him but want better Representatives in Congress: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wesleybell-nqr](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/83005984-58ce-405d-80a3-ad5ae2d3461c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
10
At some point, I may offer thoughts on who Democrats and independents can vote for in Missouri's Republican primaries. I won't for now, in large part because doing so--being a Democrat offering a Republican primary endorsement--would be detrimental to this whole idea.
If I do so, it will probably be the night before or the morning of, too late for any opposition to mobilize against it.
11
Sometimes, Democrats talk about organizing to support the most flawed Republican candidate, in hopes that said crazy Republican turns off moderate voters and is therefore more beatable. (There was some discussion around Democrats supporting Eric Greitens' Senate campaign in 2022 for this very reason.) Yes, that does sometimes happen--in the [2018 Kansas gubernatorial election](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5613a828-a6c2-4d44-acef-ec308a28fd11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), for instance, when a moderate Democrat won over a particularly loony Republican. But I think it's a very bad idea for a lot of reasons, chief among them: be careful what you wish for, because you might get it.
I don't care for Senator Eric Schmitt, but he's certainly better than a Senator Eric Greitens would've been. And realistically, that's what would've happened.
12
Unscientifically, I'm leaving off states like Colorado, Minnesota, Virginia, and Wisconsin, competitive states where the results of general elections are not foregone conclusions.

Fellow Conservative,

On Sunday, I debated my Democratic opponent, Jon Tester, and the outcome of our tete-a-tete was straightforward: it’s time for a change in Washington. The type of change I’m talking about is generational, transformative, and substantial.

This debate made clear that while Tester has spent the last 18 years in Washington talking about ‘fighting’ for voters, our problems keep worsening as American families face skyrocketing price increases in food, housing, and energy.

This debate made clear that while Tester has spent 18 years cultivating relationships with powerful D.C. lobbyists, Montanans continue to be subject to a wide-open border that allows illegal immigrants to invade our country and bring crime and drugs into our communities.

**[I’m asking for your financial support today. Let me tell you why.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=7478b139a9bc4ba0acce2f5856b6bf85&_e=gmQ6aGKKEssLQCRzz4Fvv2LoHFxAiXJGjBrX3zIlYYr5YzGg_P8x3hvdZMrBTLQHSGNVQrMzMyYEDdmqcAtONgPzon3Lntphq3ITRQs9bA_aAOFNGwEeRgmlZ9qtZmbrrcyxSbubUibOek1gWdvFy7KIOxBgKpVK6TpNQIg0_aI_EkgWBDY__X40oDEyRTx2Ovx39xxyXkEg_sbhuRpJrujr3YKBqqxzKOyDIYUiIQW8G7pBcNPVA5aGry8woEdGkY4zaUoTC-PbUINXSc4C4DB3GaOJblWa2OE60GsufvHiIGZbl_-SQ2x0sbo2oetn5F9WAF8JLyd_zrTgaR8g1auidMiPDpGZafXH6pjvTuS8KJeeFmsR94a4i-5IPCzd6NqHcsAO5AxstV_64M3fu_6dCitTadgvT-22A-bSiz4%3D)**

There are now less than five months until Election Day, and recent polling shows that whoever wins on November 5th will do so by the slimmest of margins.

**[I need your help to expose my opponent for the flip-flopping and conniving politician he truly is.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=7478b139a9bc4ba0acce2f5856b6bf85&_e=gmQ6aGKKEssLQCRzz4Fvv2LoHFxAiXJGjBrX3zIlYYr5YzGg_P8x3hvdZMrBTLQHSGNVQrMzMyYEDdmqcAtONgPzon3Lntphq3ITRQs9bA_aAOFNGwEeRgmlZ9qtZmbrrcyxSbubUibOek1gWdvFy7KIOxBgKpVK6TpNQIg0_aI_EkgWBDY__X40oDEyRTx2Ovx39xxyXkEg_sbhuRpJrujr3YKBqqxzKOyDIYUiIQW8G7pBcNPVA5aGry8woEdGu_WvwfgipuE9myuy08kjcGk8lh6KIZ4K1kVGVO8OmFL_4QLmaJMR8u53jxtGAna5iH6anUGoM8jjwDukxb68Vdwtx_2Ra7xrdqKZ0MC_kdWtkkbVR4gp17tpjfZ-eyVfta2Y1vGgG8sXyZOt_dRqfV-XMGUw5Zcv0p1o8Rkt0uM%3D)**

Peter, We just learned that the Democrats are suing to kick us off the ballot in Nevada - after we submitted nearly _three times_ the signatures required. In my experience as a candidate and as Chair of the Democratic National Committee, I know that no one jumps out of bed and shouts "Today is the day I am going to make my first donation to a political campaign or organization!" I am sure you weren't considering it today either. **But that is what I am going to ask you to do today -- to make a contribution to the DNC.** $7. Consider it for a moment? $7 if you know that Trump's record fundraising post-verdict combined with close polls means winning the White House is no sure thing. $7 if you know that losing just one Democratic-held Senate seat or a few House races we can win puts both chambers of Congress at risk of Republican control. $7 if you know that the Democratic National Committee is the organization best positioned to make a difference in these races and more. Our average online donation is around $30. Some give less. Many give more. All that matters is that you are chipping in at this critical moment to ensure we have the resources to win this November. Here's what we were up against, and how a few of these incredible women can make history in November: Indigenous activist Angel Charley defeated former state Sen. Clemente Sanchez in New Mexico's 30th state Senate District, and will become the first woman to ever represent this district if she wins in November. Navajo attorney Michelle Paulene Abeyeta defeated state Rep. Harry Garcia in New Mexico's 69th state House District, and would become the first woman and the first Indigenous person to represent this majority Native American district. STEM advocate Anita Gonzales defeated state Rep. Ambrose Castellano in New Mexico's 70th state House District, and would be the first woman and woman of color to represent this district since 1970. In New Mexico's 15th state Senate District, policy analyst and finance consultant Heather Berghmans defeated Rep. Daniel Ivey-Soto, a 10-year veteran of the New Mexico state Legislature accused by multiple women of sexual harassment and other abuse. Team — I had to make a tough decision earlier today. Let me catch you up: Jason is facing his final FEC deadline before the primary tonight. This is the most important deadline of our campaign yet, and it comes right as folks see Jason’s name on the ballot for the first time this year. I had a meeting with Jason’s Finance Director where if we had just a few more bucks, we could reach more undecided voters before the June 25 primary. **These are Coloradans that could decide some toss-up races in November.** There wasn’t money allocated in the budget, but I gave the thumbs up. I know the risk — but with Donald Trump and Lauren Boebert going all-in to win in Colorado, I couldn’t let us fall behind this early on. I’m hoping that grassroots donors can help us make up that **$2,684 budget shortfall** — just like you always have. Friend, In their endorsement of Justin this week, the Detroit Free Press Editorial Board called out Justin's primary opponent Mike Rogers for his "transactional approach to politics" and "ideological inconsistency." Sounds about right. **But if there's one thing Mike Rogers has been consistent about throughout his career, it's his desire to expand government power at the expense of your individual rights.** **Don't take our word for it. After Mark won in 2020, we had to go straight back into campaigning. He was up for re-election in 2022 for a full term in the U.S. Senate, and running two back-to-back campaigns isn’t easy.
#

Friends, we’ll be honest with you.
After Mark won in 2020, we had to go straight back into campaigning. He was up for re-election in 2022 for a full term in the U.S. Senate, and running two back-to-back campaigns isn’t easy.
We weren’t sure if we’d be able to raise what we needed to win after how expensive and tough the 2020 cycle was.
But thanks to the efforts of this team Mark won — not just in 2020, but again in 2022.
We’ve still got a ton of work to do, though. Whether that’s building and supporting teams that can win again in Arizona in 2024, helping out our friends in tough races around the country so we can hold the Senate and win back the House, or building the long-term infrastructure we need to win in the future.
This team never stopped working.
And one of the main ways we fund that work is through sustaining donations made by our top supporters. Recurring monthly donations make up almost half of our total fundraising every month, and it’s a critical pillar in our program. One we plan around each and every month.
Unfortunately, those sustaining donations have started to fall off. It’s straining our budget, and it could have larger impacts on what we’re able to do in this election cycle — and beyond.
You’ve been with us for a long time. And we were hoping that you might be able to commit to a sustaining, monthly donation. You’d be counted among Mark Kelly’s most dedicated supporters, and you would be giving him the ability to go all in as we fight for victory in Arizona and beyond in 2024.
So, how about it:
[**Can you join the thousands of others who make a monthly donation to Mark Kelly’s campaign? Use this link and make a recurring donation. It’d mean a lot to us, and to Mark.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/2349?c0=mek-em-june24.3TS_l3&refcode=em240613-1-90&t=1&akid=5782%2E6688874%2E9yQejM)

Thank you for considering it. This would be a huge help to us.
Team Kelly

subject: Your Bi-Weekly NPP eBlast
body:
| | |
---
Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New Pennsylvania Project newsletter! In this edition, you'll find critical election news, updates on upcoming and recent events, and exciting career opportunities. We’re here to keep you informed about our progress in breaking down voting barriers, key election updates, and the initiatives shaping Pennsylvania's future.

We also address how unfair the proposed Pennsylvania budget is and how it threatens to direct funding away from our communities so the rich can get richer. This budget and the headlines in the news are a reminder of why we must continue our efforts at all levels—on the streets and in the courts—to protect our rights and our communities. Freedom and liberation are projects in progress, not a destination we have reached.

As we gear up for the 2024 general election, we invite you to join us in our mission to educate and mobilize voters who then vote every election to make change in our communities.
Stay informed with essential election resources and dates as we approach the 2024 General Election on November 5th. Remember, your voice matters, and we’re here to provide the information and resources needed to shape Pennsylvania’s future.

Thank you for staying informed and engaged! Together change is possible.
---
---
|
---
**Happy Pride Month! **

At NPP, we stand strong with the LGBTQIA+ community and all impacted communities in the ongoing fight for equality and civil rights.

Voting is a critical weapon in this fight, and we're here to ensure every voice is heard and every right is protected.

This month, as we celebrate both Pride and Juneteenth, we recognize the importance of activism, hard work, and relentless advocacy in protecting our communities. We will be present at many events engaging in crucial conversations about securing the rights of everyone in our community.

On June 3rd, PA House Speaker Joanna McClinton introduced a bill (H.B. 2369) to allow two weeks of early in-person voting on machines and to authorize same-day voter registration. More than 70 lawmakers co-sponsored her bill, which has been referred to a House Committee. This is a significant step forward in making voting more accessible for all Pennsylvanians. Early in-person voting would help reduce wait times at polls and give more options for those with work or family obligations on election day. Same-day voter registration would allow voters to register and vote on election day, improving access and ensuring all voices are heard. Let’s make sure every PA voter can freely and easily access the polls to have their voices heard and their votes count. clean_body: | | | Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New Pennsylvania Project newsletter! In this edition, you'll find critical election news, updates on upcoming and recent events, and exciting career opportunities. We’re here to keep you informed about our progress in breaking down voting barriers, key election updates, and the initiatives shaping Pennsylvania's future. We also address how unfair the proposed Pennsylvania budget is and how it threatens to direct funding away from our communities so the rich can get richer. This budget and the headlines in the news are a reminder of why we must continue our efforts at all levels—on the streets and in the courts—to protect our rights and our communities. Freedom and liberation are projects in progress, not a destination we have reached. As we gear up for the 2024 general election, we invite you to join us in our mission to educate and mobilize voters who then vote every election to make change in our communities. Stay informed with essential election resources and dates as we approach the 2024 General Election on November 5th. Remember, your voice matters, and we’re here to provide the information and resources needed to shape Pennsylvania’s future. Thank you for staying informed and engaged! Together change is possible. | Happy Pride Month! At NPP, we stand strong with the LGBTQIA+ community and all impacted communities in the ongoing fight for equality and civil rights. Voting is a critical weapon in this fight, and we're here to ensure every voice is heard and every right is protected. This month, as we celebrate both Pride and Juneteenth, we recognize the importance of activism, hard work, and relentless advocacy in protecting our communities. We will be present at many events engaging in crucial conversations about securing the rights of everyone in our community. Let’s continue to build a democracy that represents and protects all of us. Love is Love. Celebrate, register, and vote. | | | | | | Exciting News! NPP is growing in Western Pennsylvania! In addition to our ongoing efforts in Allegheny County, we are thrilled to announce our new presence in Beaver, Lawrence, and Erie counties. We are committed to educating and engaging voters, building power, and supporting change in impacted communities. Our mission is to ensure every voice is heard and every vote counts. Together, we can make a difference and create a more inclusive and representative democracy. Join us in this journey as we work to empower voters and bring about lasting change in Western PA! | On June 3rd, PA House Speaker Joanna McClinton introduced a bill (H.B. 2369) to allow two weeks of early in-person voting on machines and to authorize same-day voter registration. More than 70 lawmakers co-sponsored her bill, which has been referred to a House Committee. This is a significant step forward in making voting more accessible for all Pennsylvanians. Early in-person voting would help reduce wait times at polls and give more options for those with work or family obligations on election day. Same-day voter registration would allow voters to register and vote on election day, improving access and ensuring all voices are heard. Let’s make sure every PA voter can freely and easily access the polls to have their voices heard and their votes count. | | | If you missed the May 31st appearance of our CEO Kadida Kenner on the Roland Martin Unfiltered show you can view it now on Youtube. Kadida and Roland discussed voting rights and the upcoming election and how we can boost Black voter turnout and protect our rights at the polls. You can find the recording here ( or ) Tune in for more news or future NPP appearances at and . | | | | | We're Hiring! Join the New Pennsylvania Project (NPP) and be a part of our mission to empower impacted, Black and other communities of color across PA. Help us support every eligible voter to feel compelled to vote. Your work will make a direct impact on civil rights, fair education funding, economic justice, and environmental stewardship. | | | | | | | | | | | | | June 14-16: Pgh Juneteenth Celebration @ Point State Park June 15: Mt Lebo Pride @ Mt Lebanon Main Park, 9a-4pJune 15: Lawrenceville Pride @ Bay 41, 12pm June 16: Queer Craft Market @ , 5pm June 16: Carnegie Library Book Sale @ CLP Oakland, 10a-4p | | | | On June 11th, the National Coalition of 100 Black Women, Inc., Philadelphia Chapter hosted a an important webinar, Advocacy 101: Adding Our Voice to the Conversation Virtual. The event featured our very own New Pennsylvania Project Chief Executive Officer, Kadida Kenner. The training provided an overview of the legislative process and ways to get involved by participating in public hearings, reaching out to legislators, using media and other advocacy strategies. Watch it . | | | | | | | | | | A Pennsylvania court affirmed the dismissal of a 2022 right-wing lawsuit that tried to decertify Lycoming County’s 2020 election results. Last week, the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania tossed out a lawsuit brought by two members of the Lycoming County Patriots who challenged the results of the county’s 2020 general election more than two years after it took place, . Pennsylvania Lancaster County Incompletely Dated Mail-in Ballots Challenge Pennsylvania Alliance for Retired Americans (PARA), a non-profit group, sued Lancaster County for rejecting mail-in ballots where voters forgot to write the last two digits of the current year on the outer envelope, . Judge Allows RNC and Pennsylvania Republicans to Defend Law Disqualifying Undated and Misdated Mail-in Ballots A Pennsylvania court allowed the Republican National Committee (RNC) and Pennsylvania Republican to intervene in a lawsuit challenging the state’s law that does not allow misdated or undated mail-in ballots to be counted, 4,400 Mail Ballots Were Rejected in PA in April’s Primary In April’s primary election, over 4,400 mail ballots were rejected because they lacked a date or had an incorrect date on their return envelopes. This issue could worsen in November with higher voter turnout because currently county election officials reject mail ballots with incorrect or missing dates, | 1 in 10 eligible U.S. voters say they can’t easily show proof of their citizenship Top Republicans are lining up behind a proposal to require proof of U.S. citizenship for voter registration in federal elections. But for millions of U.S. citizens, it’s not easy to prove their citizenship with a document, . Jay-Z’s Support of the Voucher Bill Draws Pushback online. He is on the Wrong side of this issue. “The AFT Pennsylvania teachers union said on the social platform X: ‘This ain’t it,’ over a photo of Jay-Z and Jeffrey Yass, a billionaire who is the biggest donor to Republican campaigns in Pennsylvania. Yass’s top issue in the state is school choice. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, a first-term Democrat, supported a Republican-backed proposal last year to send $100 million to families for private school tuition and school supplies. Shapiro later backed down in the face of House Democratic opposition.” Pa. House takes first step to make fair education funding plan into law Pennsylvania school districts would save more than $500 million a year under a proposal to set a statewide tuition rate for cyber charter schools that’s part of state House Democrats’ education plan, PA House Democrats pass historic education funding bill “This bill reflects a historic moment for public education in Pennsylvania. The state representatives who have crafted it are true leaders in the fight to fix our unconstitutionally broken public school funding system,” Pennsylvania State Education Association President Aaron Chapin said in a statement. Black leaders, state legislators rally in Harrisburg to pass CROWN Act Pennsylvania House Democrats joined leaders in the Black community last Tuesday to call on the Senate to advance the CROWN Act and ban discrimination on how hair is worn by people, especially women, of color, Gun control measures advance out of Democratic-controlled Pennsylvania House committee Democrats in majority control of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives advanced several gun control measures Wednesday, including one that would ban sales of automatic and semi-automatic guns, after years of standstill in the politically divided state government, Senate Republicans vote against making contraception a federal right The Senate voted to block a bill to create a federal right to contraception access after many Republicans said they opposed the legislation as unnecessary and government overreach, . Election officials, retired lawmakers plead for more money to protect voting Election security should not be a partisan issue. Increasingly, though, polls show that the support the president once enjoyed among these voting blocs has not only eroded, it continues to diminish over issues a world away, like the war in Gaza and at home with the high cost of living, The Sad History of Pennsylvania's Inability To Pass a Budget In the past 20 years, Pennsylvania has only passed seven budgets on time. This Pride Month and every month, Their Future PAC proudly supports our young LGBTQ+ communities. But we live in a world where a lot of adults — particularly those in positions of power and influence — actively work to demonize their identities and attack their fundamental right to exist.

Here are the facts (source: _The Trevor Project_):
* **_45%_** of LGBTQ+ youth have seriously contemplated suicide in the past year (rates are higher for transgender and nonbinary youth and youth of color).
* **_Fewer than 1 in 3_** transgender and nonbinary youth found their home to be gender-affirming.
* **_60%_** of LGBTQ youth who wanted mental health care in the past year were not able to get it.

While the GOP is outlawing gender-affirming healthcare — a medical necessity that saves lives — we’re working to find and elect leaders who will make our kids feel seen and supported.

name: Victoria Spartz
subject: MAGGIE’S LIST ENDORSES SPARTZ
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/spartzforcongress/spartz-wins-republican-primary-17382284?e=57d5bacdc3)
---
| |
---
| | Dear Friends,

This week, I was honored to be endorsed by **Maggie’s List, **a political action committee dedicated to electing fiscally conservative women to office. Being a woman in politics is not easy, but being a conservative woman is really hard. However, I’ll always stand with you and fight for you against the Washington insiders.

Warmest wishes,
Victoria

P.S. See excerpts of the Maggie’s List’s press release below:

“We are pleased to endorse Victoria Spartz for Congress in Indiana’s 5th Congressional District,” said Maggie’s List Founder and Chair, Sandra Mortham. “Victoria is a true champion for the Maggie’s List values of strong national security, fiscal responsibility and limited government. A natural leader, we are proud to support her re-election effort and are grateful for her willingness to serve,“ Mortham continued.

In an era of politicians with sound bites, Congresswoman Spartz is a policy leader who is already made a legislative difference even in her first two terms—12 bills signed into law and many policies developed from scratch. She is also known for her work holding the Biden Administration accountable.

She has been named Commissioner to the U.S. Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe (known as the Helsinki Commission). She serves on the Judiciary Committee, Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust, as well as the Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement.

Lowering health care costs have also been a large part of her policy agenda. She received the “Champion of Healthcare Innovation” award from the Healthcare Leadership Council and helped pass HR 5378 Lower Cost, More Transparency Act.

Her other accomplishments include working to reduce dependencies on China and increase transparency into the Chinese publicly traded companies and enhancing border security _(H.R.2) _and designate cartels as a Foreign Terrorist Organization.

#
Peter,
This morning, a former chief justice of the Missouri Supreme Court said Missouri law puts IVF at risk. He said we need new legislation from Congress to protect it.
**But this afternoon, Josh Hawley voted against the Right to IVF Act anyway.**

name: Joe Pereles for Missouri
subject: Protect IVF and contraception
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pereles for Missouri, Rhonda West, Treasurer
body:
https://www.perelesformissouri.com/ [https://www.perelesformissouri.com/]
Peter,
If you think the basic right to have autonomy over your reproductive health care decisions is increasingly at risk due to the overturning of Roe v. Wade, wait—there is more. And it gets even worse, if that is possible.
When Roe was overturned by the Supreme Court in 2022, abortions were completely banned in Missouri with vague exceptions to “save the life of the mother.” But this denial of personal choice is only the beginning.
Now Republicans are brazenly preparing to limit or eliminate access to contraception and in-vitro fertilization (IVF). These threats have nothing to do with the real needs of Missourians, but simply fall in line with a national MAGA agenda to take away personal freedom and maximize government control over personal choices. We saw the fallout from a judicial decision in Alabama that forbids access to IVF. There is nothing to stop this from happening here.
Our own U.S. Senators have already begun undermining such freedoms. Senators Josh Hawley and Eric Schmitt, both Republicans who claim to be pro-family and in favor of limited government, voted against a bill that would ensure a right to contraceptives for anyone who wants or needs it.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perelesformissouri24?refcode=ivf [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perelesformissouri24?refcode=ivf]
I believe that we must safeguard reproductive rights and protect our fundamental right to privacy. Every individual should have control over their own lives and bodies, and the right to plan if, when, or how to start a family.
Reckless extremists with radical and unpopular views about contraception and IVF have no place making laws that cause chaos, uncertainty, and emotional turmoil for women and families.
The lack of action by the Missouri legislature and the failure by our GOP Senators to enshrine protections for contraception access is alarming. As your State Senator, I will fight to protect IVF and guarantee access to fertility treatment.
Winning this seat is crucial to putting an end to the chaos and extremism that endangers basic reproductive rights and puts lives at risk. We can do more than just stop bad legislation if we flip this seat: we can take proactive steps to protect access to IVF and contraception.
Can I count on you to support this campaign and help me stand up for our rights in Jefferson City? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perelesformissouri24?refcode=ivf]
DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perelesformissouri24?refcode=ivf]
Thank you for never giving up the fight for our basic freedoms and rights. There is so much at stake, and I know that we will win together.
Sincerely,
Joe

I am pleased to share some important news regarding access to reproductive health care.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/86841327/479198910/-201694504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzOWFlM2Y4OS1jMjI5LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Y7t_XkJ_7U5MhIgWnOTXlL9gFI87tcDkvW9-kOBagi8=&emci=3532ef82-c229-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=39ae3f89-c229-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=9494239)

| | **The Supreme Court has unanimously ruled to preserve access to mifepristone, a medication used in nearly two-thirds of all abortions in the United States.** This is the first case related to abortion since the Supreme Court's decision to overturn _Roe v. Wade_ two years ago. That decision has radically constrained reproductive freedom in frightening and dangerous ways; in 26 states and counting, automatic trigger laws turned abortion from a legal procedure to a criminalized act in an instant. Because of this, many were awaiting this morning's holding bracing for another blow to our basic constitutional rights of liberty, privacy, and equality. But today, we awoke to a welcome surprise: **the Supreme Court determined that abortion opponents did not have the legal right to challenge the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) approval of mifepristone.** In doing so, the Court upheld the current accessibility of this critical medication. This ruling also reinforces the FDA's authority in the drug approval process, a crucial victory for the scientific integrity of the FDA. While today we can breathe a sigh of relief, it is important to acknowledge that abortion access remains under attack by far-right extremists. Washington is one of 16 states with laws that protect abortion rights, but in many states where abortion is banned or heavily regulated, the preservation of mifepristone does not alleviate the substantial challenges faced by individuals seeking abortions. **After all, Republican leaders have promised that they will seek a nationwide abortion ban if they take over Congress in November.** As a member of Congress with a 100% voting record on choice, endorsed many times by Planned Parenthood, I will fight hard to codify abortion rights nationwide in federal law. Last fall, I joined a majority in the House to pass the Women's Health Protection Act, which would do exactly that. But it is currently being blocked by Republicans in the Senate. clean_body: I am pleased to share some important news regarding access to reproductive health care. | | | | The Supreme Court has unanimously ruled to preserve access to mifepristone, a medication used in nearly two-thirds of all abortions in the United States. This is the first case related to abortion since the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade two years ago. That decision has radically constrained reproductive freedom in frightening and dangerous ways; in 26 states and counting, automatic trigger laws turned abortion from a legal procedure to a criminalized act in an instant. Because of this, many were awaiting this morning's holding bracing for another blow to our basic constitutional rights of liberty, privacy, and equality. But today, we awoke to a welcome surprise: the Supreme Court determined that abortion opponents did not have the legal right to challenge the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) approval of mifepristone. In doing so, the Court upheld the current accessibility of this critical medication. This ruling also reinforces the FDA's authority in the drug approval process, a crucial victory for the scientific integrity of the FDA. While today we can breathe a sigh of relief, it is important to acknowledge that abortion access remains under attack by far-right extremists. Washington is one of 16 states with laws that protect abortion rights, but in many states where abortion is banned or heavily regulated, the preservation of mifepristone does not alleviate the substantial challenges faced by individuals seeking abortions. **I’m running for Congress to restore what I call The Michigan Dream:** that if you work hard, you can own a home, pay your bills, put a little away for retirement, and maybe drive your family to Disney World every now and then.

I know this dream firsthand. Growing up in Portland, my dad worked construction, often clocking in 70 to 80 hours a week. When the construction season slowed down and it got cold, he worked snow removal to make ends meet. Like many people in this district, he showered at the end of his work day, not before it. Dad wasn’t afraid to get calluses on his hands through a tough day’s work. Thanks to him and my mom, my sisters and I were the first in our family to go to college, and I have been working to uplift families like ours ever since.

**Unfortunately, today, the Michigan Dream has become out-of-reach for too many Michiganders.** Combine that with extremists making us less safe by trying to take away the right to abortion and refusing to address the epidemic of gun violence, and it’s clear that we need to send real leaders to D.C. who we can trust to solve problems our community faces.

I have spent my adult life fighting to make it just a little easier for working families, like the one I grew up in, to achieve the Michigan Dream. Throughout my career and now in the state Senate, I’ve helped improve employment and educational opportunities for children across our state, pass historic tax cuts for working families, and enact public policy that’s helped level the playing field.

**I’m running for Congress because I am ready to help give hardworking families across the Great Lakes Bay Region the tools to succeed.**

clean_body: We have an opportunity to push President Biden to deliver on his promise to keep families together. Hi Peter, We have an opportunity to push President Biden to deliver on his promise to keep families together. With one signature, he can extend work permits to an estimated 1.3 million people who are undocumented spouses of American citizens. Many of these people are care workers and family caregivers, and they deserve to live with the safety of being home without the threat of separation and deportation. Living with the threat of being separated from their families is a nightmare scenario for undocumented spouses. Many of them are care workers and caregivers who are critical to the care infrastructure in our country — supporting their own families and the families they care for. Granting work permits for undocumented spouses married to US citizens is an executive action that would not require congressional approval. It would show people who have built their lives here, and their loved ones, that America recognizes the incredibly important role they play in our society. Thank you for taking action, Care in Action

They’re now proposing _the death penalty_ for abortion patients and the doctors who perform them. Doesn’t sound very “pro-life” to me!

– _Newsweek_
There’s no way around it: these people are straight up fascists, and the future of our democracy and all of our rights depends on defeating them.
**[Will you rush an urgent donation of $5 or more to help us elect young progressives who will fight to stop extremism and defend reproductive rights?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240613-1?refcode=em20240613-1&amount=5&refcode2=803_587540__u28G5&akid=803%2E587540%2E_u28G5)**
It’s almost unreal. To think that a political party which holds all the levers of power in the second most populous state in the country could **_murder people_** for seeking abortions is terrifying.
**But they actually proposed it as a plank to their party platform at the end of May.**
This just makes it all the more clear how urgent it is that we help our Leaders We Deserve endorsed candidates in Texas win this year. And I’m committed to doing everything I can to make certain that happens.
**Molly Cook** in Houston has already won a special election to fill the remainder of the current term in the Texas Senate, but she’ll need to win again this November to serve a full term. She’s currently the most progressive member of the Senate, and it’s crucial that she remain there to keep fighting for abortion rights.
In the Dallas area, **Averie Bishop** has made abortion rights a central part of her campaign for the State House. She has an opportunity to flip a red district blue and make real progress toward actually flipping the legislature — but she needs our help to do it.
This fight won’t be easy, but with Republicans literally proposing the state-sanctioned murder of doctors and abortion patients, **_losing isn’t an option._**

And I’m committed to doing everything I can to make certain that happens. Molly Cook in Houston has already won a special election to fill the remainder of the current term in the Texas Senate, but she’ll need to win again this November to serve a full term. She’s currently the most progressive member of the Senate, and it’s crucial that she remain there to keep fighting for abortion rights. In the Dallas area, Averie Bishop has made abortion rights a central part of her campaign for the State House. She has an opportunity to flip a red district blue and make real progress toward actually flipping the legislature — but she needs our help to do it. This fight won’t be easy, but with Republicans literally proposing the state-sanctioned murder of doctors and abortion patients, losing isn’t an option. More soon, David Hogg

| Peter,

I know what it’s like to be underestimated.

As a young mom of two girls (Mae and Evie), I faced the overwhelming challenge of caring for them and my husband Matt, who struggled with post-traumatic stress while navigating the bureaucratic barriers that military families often face.

I was often frustrated and discouraged, and there were times when I felt like we were just too poor or working class to ever be important. That feeling—of being nothing while giving what we felt was everything—motivated me to do whatever it took to have a voice, not just for ourselves** but for the people we loved and cared about.**

I worked with military non-profits, earned a law degree, and helped veterans take on the VA for free.

When I first announced my campaign for Congress a little over a year ago, I was met with skepticism. Lots of it. Who thinks they can challenge a four-term incumbent? I can. _**Because this is my home.**_ My roots go back five generations here. And I know what it’s like to fight with your back against the wall - like lives depend on it. Because the simple truth is they do. It’s why I’ll never play political games: this is my community - the place that taught Matt and me everything we know about who we are and what we’re about.

I’ve traveled across the district and have had countless conversations with folks here who feel let down by Jack Bergman. They have been. Jack Bergman isn’t from here. He’s not committed to this district, to our families, to our way of life.

We know we can unseat him and bring real representation to this district, but we’ll need your help.

[_**At the end of the month, Jack Bergman and his allies will be paying close attention to our fundraising. We have to show him we have the momentum to unseat him. Friend: Have you seen all the _horrible_ things Rick Scott has been up to?

There's been a lot. But here's a quick summary for you:
* **Scott proudly supported the abortion ban in Florida,** which went into effect on May 1.
* He skipped a crucial FAA reauthorization vote to support his good friend Donald Trump in court, **even going as far as attacking Judge Merchan’s daughter in front of the courthouse.**
* After overseeing one of the largest Medicare frauds in history, stealing **MILLIONS** of dollars from Medicare and using that same money to buy his way into the Senate seat he currently occupies — _**he's playing the victim**. _
* And just days after he accompanied Trump in court, he announced that he's officially running to be the next Senate Republican leader.** This means my race to retire Rick Scott could decide BOTH the Senate majority and the majority leader.**

But enough is enough. **_Ya no más_**. Scott’s time of wasting taxpayer money in the Senate ends now. Floridians deserve a real leader, friend, not someone who's only interested in winning Trump's approval by being his mouthpiece while he's under a gag order.
Unlike Rick, I got into public service because I truly care about people**.** After years of seeing the harm he's done in Florida, and how it’s only getting worse, I knew it was time to fight back and stand up for Floridians. **That's why I'm promising to use my voice in the Senate to fight for affordable health care, protect the critical government programs and benefits that Rick Scott wants to gut, and defend reproductive freedom nationwide.**
